guard: the session-start hook hands the seat its orientation card at every SessionStart, or with the next prompt when the seat was not bound at the start, and hands an owed card over once
why: The briefing in the system prompt tells the model to orient; the card is the orienting. A model
that has to ask spends its first turn on it, and after a compaction it has forgotten the answer
while the instruction survived. The hook is the only place that fires on both.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed. The suite imports the handle by RELATIVE SOURCE
PATH (../src/hooks.js), so the bytes mutated are the bytes graded. Its package-name imports
(MeshAgent, the types, the sentinel) carry no behaviour under test.
K1 is the plain omission. K2 is the race that a startup hook loses: SessionStart arrives before
the broker bind, so a card not owed to the next prompt is a card never handed over. K3 is the
owed flag that never clears, which hands the card over with every prompt for the rest of the

mutations.expectRed: a bound session start hands over the orientation card
mutations.cell: a bound session start hands over the orientation card

mutations.name: K2 an owed card is never delivered
mutations.find: const parts = [cardOwed ? await orientation() : undefined, surfaceAutomatic(agent, ev),
mutations.expectRed: an unbound session start owes the card to the next prompt
mutations.cell: an unbound session start owes the card to the next prompt

mutations.name: K3 the owed flag never clears
mutations.expectRed: the owed card is handed over once
mutations.cell: the owed card is handed over once
